MCD.rationale: McDonald's demonstrates solid fundamental health with a dominant franchise model (~95% franchised), industry-leading operating margins (~45-46%), and strong brand moat. Q1 2026 showed 9% YoY revenue growth and 7% EPS growth, with 3.8% global comparable sales growth. However, the stock faces headwinds: QoQ metrics show sequential deceleration (revenue -7.9%, EPS -12.6%), rising oil prices ($100/bbl) pressuring lower-income consumer spending, and the CEO warned conditions could be 'getting a little bit worse.' The stock has declined ~14% over the past quarter from $329 to $284, and at a P/E of ~23 (lowest in nearly two years per Investing.com), valuation appears more reasonable versus its own history. The negative equity position (-$1.29B) reflects the company's leveraged capital structure but is structural to the franchise/real estate model. Near-term catalysts are limited: Q2 faces tough comparisons from the prior-year Minecraft promotion, and management guided for weaker sales. The dividend of $1.86/share (yield ~2.6%) and 49 consecutive years of increases provide support. Overall, a quality defensive franchise at a more attractive valuation than recent history, but macro headwinds and decelerating trends limit upside conviction.
